## Project overview

I designed and built this portfolio as a production-style Docusaurus documentation site to demonstrate documentation engineering, docs-as-code workflows, React/MDX customisation, automated QA, and CI/CD.

The portfolio includes:

* Technical writing skills and documentation tools
* Case studies of previous projects
* Markdown and MDX content
* Autogenerated landing pages under `skills/` and `tools/`
* React and JSX components for reusable presentation
* Mermaid diagrams
* Automated documentation QA and GitHub Pages deployment

The QA pipeline combines:

* **DeepSeek AI** for higher-level editorial and portfolio review
* **AccessibilityCheck** for issues such as alt text, vague links, and heading structure
* **LinkCheck** for local links and assets
* **Remark** for Markdown/MDX syntax and structure checks
* **Vale** for mechanical style-guide and terminology rules
* **Lychee** for external link checking
* **LTeX+** as a front end for **LanguageTool** for spelling, punctuation, and grammar checking

The checks are combined into HTML and JSON reports and run automatically when anyone pushes changes to the site using GitHub Actions.

## The challenge

The project gave me an opportunity to:

* Learn Docusaurus, React/JSX, and GitHub Actions
* Build a technical-writing portfolio using docs-as-code practices
* Integrate an LLM API into an automated QA workflow
* Combine AI review with deterministic linting, accessibility, style, and link checks

## My approach

I treated the portfolio as a small documentation product rather than a collection of static pages.

Docusaurus provides the documentation framework, with Markdown and MDX used for content and React components added where reusable presentation logic is useful.

GitHub Actions automate deployment and QA. A Python QA script coordinates AI review and deterministic checks, validates AI findings against the source, and generates a unified report containing issues and suggested improvements.

The pipeline can run locally or in CI and supports per-page and site-wide review. CI thresholds can fail the workflow for serious documentation problems while still allowing the QA report to be generated and published for investigation.

I also created reusable components for skills, tools, and marketing-style content while keeping the authoring experience Markdown-first.

## Deliverables

* This Docusaurus portfolio, published on GitHub Pages
* A [Documentation QA report](pathname:///qa/) for the current site
* The GitHub repository containing the source, QA tooling, and deployment workflow

## Outcome

The result is a maintainable portfolio that demonstrates a modern docs-as-code workflow, reusable documentation components, automated deployment, and a multi-layer documentation QA pipeline.
